baseline_models.focus_anchor: The whole ayah is the standalone rootless two-letter form حمٓ.
baseline_models.mechanism: Two recited letter names make a bounded sound event without lexical predication. Their opacity suspends semantic commitment while their isolation marks a discourse threshold.

changed_reading.after: A deliberately non-propositional acoustic threshold that makes the hearer wait for what follows.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate sequel joins delivery to ordered writing. That adjacency revises the isolated letter-sound into a compact header at the boundary where a transmitted book becomes audible discourse.

activation_trace.role: Caused descent and delivery supply the message's movement toward its audience and make the preceding sound a point of arrival.
Ordered letters and the name of what is written supply the articulated textual body that follows the rootless letter pair.

structural_cues: 40:1 is a complete rootless ayah immediately followed by 40:2's nominal statement of the book's descent.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate adjacency, delivery, and letters ordered as writing; I infer that the ayah boundary makes حمٓ an audible header for that delivery. It may instead remain an independent section marker.

changed_reading.after: A delivery header: a compact audible threshold through which the written message begins to arrive.

context_deltas.mechanism: The bare ح-م sequence is repeatedly re-embedded in rooted words. One clustered ayah differentiates it through carrying, praise, and mercy; later the doubled-m form حميم branches between intimate nearness and hot water. The opening can therefore function as an underdetermined consonantal kernel whose completions traverse support, valuation, care, failed closeness, and heat.

activation_trace.role: Visible carrying extends the focus sequence with ل and supplies the kernel's burden-bearing development.
Praise as the opposite of blame extends the same sequence with د and supplies its evaluative development.
Mercy and tenderness place ر before the focus sequence and supply its caring relational development.
Kinship and nearness resolve the doubled-m form as intimate support precisely where that support is denied.
Hot water resolves the same doubled-m form materially as heat, reversing relational closeness into exposure.

structural_cues: 40:7 clusters حمل, حمد, and رحمة in one ayah, three distinct roots containing the focus's contiguous ح-م sequence.
The same حميم surface occurs at 40:18 in a denied-support construction and at 40:72 beside fire and stoking.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the occurrences and distinct branch domains; I align their exact ح-م sequence with the focus and treat added or doubled radicals as differentiation. Common consonantal overlap remains a live alternative, so this is not a claim of lexical derivation.

changed_reading.before: Two letters withholding a lexical reading.
changed_reading.after: A latent consonantal kernel that the surah repeatedly roots into sharply different material and relational outcomes.

context_deltas.mechanism: The letter names require voicing without yet yielding a sentence. The surah later contrasts futile calling with a call answered in the next word, strengthening the opening's possible function as a minimal summons in which responsive attention precedes propositional decoding.

activation_trace.role: Calling and drawing by speech supply the failed-call pole of the surah's response pattern.
Direct calling by speech supplies the successful summons pole.
Reply to speech supplies the immediate answering movement that completes the summons.

structural_cues: 40:50 moves through repeated speech into futile call and calling, whereas 40:60 places 'call Me' and 'I answer' in adjacent words 3-4.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opposed call outcomes and an adjacent call-answer pair; I assign the recited but nonlexical حمٓ a summons function. It may instead mark the text without soliciting a response.

changed_reading.before: A sound that merely marks an opening.
changed_reading.after: A minimal summons whose first meaning is the listener's obligation to attend and answer.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it maps Arabic articulation onto body imagery, a reader-supplied phonetic bridge rather than packet semantics. It remains anchored in the actual ح-to-م oral sequence and is supported by the throat and held-silence branches at 40:18; downstream prose should present it only as an acoustic possibility, not a lexical decoding.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: In oral realization, the focus begins with pharyngeal ح and ends its second letter-name on bilabial م.

activation_trace.role: The throat as an articulatory location supplies a bodily origin against which the initial ح can be heard.
Held breath and silence supply closure against which the final bilabial م can be heard.

changed_reading.before: A visually opaque pair of named letters.
changed_reading.after: A miniature embodied passage from throat onset to held lip closure, acoustically anticipating the surah's choking scene.

strongest_changes: Immediate adjacency to delivered, ordered writing turns the opening into an audible delivery header.
The 40:7 cluster and the two حميم occurrences activate حمٓ as a consonantal kernel with divergent relational and material completions.
Contrasted failed and answered calls make the nonlexical utterance function as a summons to responsive attention.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah scope exposed a concentrated ح-م cluster at 40:7 and a closeness-to-heat reversal across 40:18 and 40:72 that a local reading would likely miss.
remaining_uncertainties: Because 40:1 is rootless, every change attaches to letter form, recitation, or ayah boundary rather than lexical morphology.
The ح-م recurrence may be functional activation or coincidental consonantal overlap; the packet cannot decide.
The throat-to-lip model depends on reader-supplied phonetics and remains exploratory.
